1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 **Script:** `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py ` scans every `core.action.script` body and every `=js:` expression for the unsupported constructs listed above, plus the script-node rules (top-level `return` of an object, no `function main()` wrapper, no `console.log`, no `aggregate` variable). None of these are caught by `uip maestro flow validate`. 542 543 --- 544 545 ## Scoping Rules 546 547 ### Node Output Availability 548 549 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 550 551 ### Loop Scope 552 553 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 554 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 555 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 556 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 557 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 558 559 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 560 561 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 562 563 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 564 565 ### Subflow Scope 566 567 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 568 569 --- 570 571 ## Variable Management via CLI 572 573 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 574 575 ### Adding a workflow input variable 576 577 1. Open `.flow` 578 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 579 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 580 581 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 582 583 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 584 585 ```json 586 { 587 "id": "myScript.output", 588 "type": "object", 589 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 590 }, 591 { 592 "id": "myScript.error", 593 "type": "object", 594 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 595 } 596 ``` 597 598 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 599 600 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 601 602 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 603 604 ```json 605 "outputs": { 606 "result": { 607 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 608 } 609 } 610 ``` 611 612 --- 613 614 ## Complete Example 615 616 A flow with input, state, and output variables: 617 618 ```json 619 { 620 "variables": { 621 "globals": [ 622 { 623 "id": "inputItems", 624 "direction": "in", 625 "type": "array", 626 "subType": "object", 627 "defaultValue": [], 628 "description": "Items to process" 629 }, 630 { 631 "id": "processedCount", 632 "direction": "inout", 633 "type": "number", 634 "defaultValue": 0 635 }, 636 { 637 "id": "result", 638 "direction": "out", 639 "type": "object", 640 "description": "Processing summary" 641 } 642 ], 643 "nodes": [ 644 { 645 "id": "transform1.output", 646 "type": "object", 647 "binding": { "nodeId": "transform1", "outputId": "output" } 648 } 649 ], 650 "variableUpdates": { 651 "transform1": [ 652 { 653 "variableId": "processedCount", 654 "expression": "=js:$vars.processedCount + $vars.transform1.output.count" 655 } 656 ] 657 } 658 }, 659 "nodes": [ 660 { 661 "id": "start", 662 "type": "core.trigger.manual", 663 "typeVersion": "1.0", 664 "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" }, 665 "inputs": { 666 "entryPointId": "" 667 }, 668 "outputs": { 669 "output": { 670 "type": "object", 671 "description": "Data passed when the flow is triggered manually.", 672 "source": "null", 673 "var": "output" 674 } 675 } 676 }, 677 { 678 "id": "transform1", 679 "type": "core.action.script", 680 "typeVersion": "1.0", 681 "inputs": { 682 "script": "const items = $vars.inputItems.filter(i => i.active);\nreturn { count: items.length, items: items };" 683 }, 684 "outputs": { 685 "output": { 686 "type": "object", 687 "description": "The return value of the script", 688 "source": "=result.response", 689 "var": "output" 690 }, 691 "error": { 692 "type": "object", 693 "description": "Error information if the script fails", 694 "source": "=Error", 695 "var": "error" 696 } 697 } 698 }, 699 { 700 "id": "end1", 701 "type": "core.control.end", 702 "typeVersion": "1.0", 703 "display": { "label": "End" }, 704 "inputs": {}, 705 "outputs": { 706 "result": { 707 "source": "=js:({ total: $vars.processedCount, data: $vars.transform1.output })" 708 } 709 } 710 } 711 ], 712 "edges": [ 713 { 714 "id": "e1", 715 "sourceNodeId": "start", 716 "sourcePort": "output", 717 "targetNodeId": "transform1", 718 "targetPort": "input" 719 }, 720 { 721 "id": "e2", 722 "sourceNodeId": "transform1", 723 "sourcePort": "success", 724 "targetNodeId": "end1", 725 "targetPort": "input" 726 } 727 ] 728 } 729 ``` 730

21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.

65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
119	
120	Example — manual start trigger:
121	
122	```json
123	{
124	  "id": "start",
125	  "type": "core.trigger.manual",
126	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
127	  "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
128	  "inputs": {
129	    "entryPointId": "3d4a8c34-5682-4ebe-a6bc-d92a18830bb5"
130	  },
131	  "outputs": {
132	    "output": { "type": "object", "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.", "source": "null", "var": "output" }
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	### Node outputs
138	
139	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
140	
141	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
142	
143	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
144	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
145	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
146	
147	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
148	
149	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
150	
151	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
152	- `description` — human-readable description
153	- `source` — runtime binding expression, copied from the manifest `outputDefinition`. `"=Error"` for errors, always.
154	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
155	
156	**Orchestrator-job nodes (api-workflow, rpa-workflow, agent, agentic-process, function): declare `error` only — `output` is derived.** They are the one family whose instance block the converter reads: it copies an authored `source` verbatim, and injects `{output, jsonSchema, "=this"}` when a non-empty `outputs` omits `output`. So `"=result.response"` there — the connector/script source — leaves `$vars.<nodeId>.output` null at runtime while `flow validate` passes. Studio Web serializes `error`-only instances too (verified on api-workflow, published-flow, and inline-agent nodes). Subflow and published-flow (`uipath.core.flow.*`) instance blocks are never read — still declare `error` only.
157	
158	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector):
159	
160	```json
161	"outputs": {
162	  "output": {
163	    "type": "object",
164	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
165	    "source": "=result.response",
166	    "var": "output"
167	  },
168	  "error": {
169	    "type": "object",
170	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
171	    "source": "=Error",
172	    "var": "error"
173	  }
174	}
175	```
176	
177	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port. A manual trigger carries the literal string `"null"` as its `source`, matching what Studio Web writes:
178	
179	```json
180	"outputs": {
181	  "output": {
182	    "type": "object",
183	    "description": "Data passed when manually triggering the process.",
184	    "source": "null",
185	    "var": "output"
186	  }
187	}
188	```
189	
190	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).
191	
192	## Layout
193	
194	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
195	
196	```json
197	"layout": {
198	  "nodes": {
199	    "start": {
200	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
201	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
202	      "collapsed": false
203	    },
204	    "rollDice": {
205	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
206	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
207	      "collapsed": false
208	    },
209	    "end": {
210	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
211	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
212	      "collapsed": false
213	    }
214	  }
215	}
216	```
217	
218	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
219	
220	**What format does:**
221	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
222	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
223	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
224	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
225	
226	**Script:** `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py <flow>` reports nodes whose `layout` entry is missing or whose `size` disagrees with the shape sizes above — the MST-9061 symptom — and `--apply` resets them to the shape sizes above; `uip maestro flow format` remains the canonical layout step.
227	
228	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).
229	
230	## Edge — both ports required
231	
232	```json
233	{
234	  "id": "edge-start-rollDice",
235	  "sourceNodeId": "start",
236	  "sourcePort": "output",
237	  "targetNodeId": "rollDice",
238	  "targetPort": "input"
239	}
240	```
241	
242	> **Gotcha**: `targetPort` is required. Omitting it produces `[error] [edges[N].targetPort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` at validate time.
243	>
244	> **Gotcha**: the source field is `sourcePort`, not `sourceHandle`. If you write `sourceHandle`, validation fails with `[error] [edges[N].sourcePort] Invalid input: expected string, received undefined` — the path identifies the offending edge entry exactly.
245	>
246	> **Gotcha — edge `id` MUST start with a letter (XML NCName).** Never use a bare UUID or any id with a leading digit (`"12bd09dd-…"`, `"1edge-start"`). Edge ids become BPMN `<bpmn:incoming>/<bpmn:outgoing>` IDREFs; a leading digit makes the converter silently drop those references while still emitting the `sequenceFlow`, so `flow validate` passes and upload succeeds — but the engine cannot traverse: the run reports **Completed having executed only the start node**, every output null. Use descriptive ids (`e-<source>-<target>`, e.g. `e-start-agent`); prefixing a letter (`e12bd09dd-…`) also works. Same rule applies to node ids.

308	## Implicit error port on action nodes
309	
310	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
311	
312	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
313	
314	### Default: off — enable only for a failure the flow actually handles
315	
316	`inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is **opt-in, and stays off unless the requirements name a failure fallback.** Turning it on suppresses the node's fault: the node returns instead of faulting and execution continues. Enable it only when both hold:
317	
318	1. The requirements state what should happen when this node fails ("if the call fails, …", "return X for invalid input", "handle timeouts") — **and**
319	2. You wire the node's `error` port to a handler that produces an outcome distinguishable from success.
320	
321	Never set the flag on a node that has no outgoing `error` edge — it suppresses the fault with nothing to catch it, converting a real failure into a run that reports success. Let the CLI own the flag: `uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set it from the error edges actually present. If you find the flag on a node with no error edge, remove it.
322	
323	### Do not swallow the failure
324	
325	An `error` edge must not rejoin the happy path. When it does, every failure walks the success route and the run reports `Completed` while the work never happened — the flow "always looks successful."
326	
327	| | Error-path target | Result |
328	| --- | --- | --- |
329	| ✗ | The next node on the happy path | Failure is invisible; downstream nodes run on missing data |
330	| ✗ | The same End node the success path reaches | Success path's output mappings run against the failed node's empty output |
331	| ✓ | A **distinct** End node mapping an error/status `out` variable | Caller can tell failure from success |
332	| ✓ | `core.logic.terminate` | Aborts the flow when recovery is impossible — see [terminate/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/terminate/impl.md) |
333	| ✓ | A recovery branch that rejoins **only after obtaining valid data** — a retry that succeeded, or a fallback source that returned data | Downstream runs on real data, not on the failed node's empty output |
334	
335	```text
336	Trigger -> HTTP Request
337	  |-- default -> Process -> End (success — status: "ok")
338	  |-- error   -> Log Error -> End (failure — status: "failed", message from $vars.httpCall.error)
339	```
340	
341	### When the error port fires
342	
343	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
344	- Request timeouts
345	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
346	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
347	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
348	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
349	
350	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`. **That is the correct default, not a defect to design around** — a faulted run is visible to the operator; a swallowed failure is not. Only trade the fault for an error path when the requirements say what that path should do.
351	
352	### Wiring the error port
353	
354	```bash
355	# Confirm the node supports error handling
356	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
357	
358	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
359	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
360	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
361	```
362	
363	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically — only for nodes that have an error edge. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself **on those nodes only**:
364	
365	```json
366	{
367	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
368	  "inputs": {
369	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
370	  }
371	}
372	```
373	
374	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
375	
376	### Error port vs other branching
377	
378	| Mechanism | When to use |
379	| --- | --- |
380	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
381	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
382	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
383	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

504	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
505	
506	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). Preserve its lifecycle-generated contents; project scaffolding creates it, and the Flow lifecycle regenerates it before execution or publication.
507	
508	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
509	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
510	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
511	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
512	
513	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.
514	
515	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
516	
517	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
518	
519	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
520	
521	```json
522	"bindings": [
523	  {
524	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
525	    "name": "name",
526	    "type": "string",
527	    "resource": "process",
528	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
529	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
530	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
531	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
532	  },
533	  {
534	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
535	    "name": "folderPath",
536	    "type": "string",
537	    "resource": "process",
538	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
539	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
540	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
541	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
542	  }
543	]
544	```
545	
546	**Rules:**
547	
548	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
549	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
550	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
551	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
552	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
553	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
554	
555	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
556	
557	**Script:** `python3 scripts/audit_flow.py <flow>` reads each resource node's definition (`model.bindings.resourceKey` / `resourceSubType` and the `<bindings.NAME>` placeholders in `model.context[]`) and reports every missing `(resourceKey, name)` entry, plus duplicates and unused entries. `--fix-plan <file>` emits them as a `flow_edit` plan and `--apply` writes them, both refusing when the definition does not supply `resource` / `resourceSubType` — in that case take the exact shape from the resource plugin's `impl.md`.
558	
559	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).
560	
561	See each resource plugin's `impl.md` for the full JSON per node type: [rpa](../author/references/plugins/rpa/impl.md), [agent](../author/references/plugins/agent/impl.md), [flow](../author/references/plugins/flow/impl.md), [agentic-process](../author/references/plugins/agentic-process/impl.md), [api-workflow](../author/references/plugins/api-workflow/impl.md), [hitl](../author/references/plugins/hitl/impl.md).
562	
563	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.
564	
565	## Bindings — connector connection binding
566	
567	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. This is configured in `content/bindings_v2.json`.
568	
569	See the relevant node guide in `nodes/` for the full `bindings_v2.json` schema, connection resource field reference, JSON examples, and the connection fetching workflow.
570

1	# Connector Activity Nodes — Implementation
2	
3	How to configure connector activity nodes: connection binding, enriched metadata, reference field resolution, and debugging. Connection bindings are emitted by `uip maestro flow node configure` into the flow's top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from them at debug/pack time and should never be hand-edited.
4	
5	For generic node/edge add, remove, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). This guide covers the connector-specific configuration workflow that must follow the generic node add.
6	
7	## How Connector Nodes Differ from OOTB
8	
9	1. **Connection binding required** — every connector node needs an IS connection (OAuth, API key, etc.) authored in the flow's top-level `bindings[]` (which the CLI regenerates into `bindings_v2.json` at debug/pack time). Without it, the node cannot authenticate.
10	2. **Enriched metadata via `--connection-id`** — call `registry get` with `--connection-id` to get connection-aware field metadata. Without it, only base fields are returned — custom fields, dynamic enums, and reference resolution are missing.
11	3. **`inputs.detail` object** — connector nodes store operation-specific configuration in `inputs.detail`, populated by `uip maestro flow node configure`:
12	   - `connectionId` — the bound IS connection UUID
13	   - `connectionFolderKey` — the Orchestrator folder key in the authored `.flow` file. `node configure --detail` accepts `folderKey` as input and writes it back as `connectionFolderKey`.
14	   - `method` — HTTP method from `registry get` → `connectorMethodInfo.method` (e.g., `POST`)
15	   - `endpoint` — API path. Read `connectorMethodInfo.path` (from `registry get`) or `availableOperations[].path` (from `is resources describe`).
16	   - `objectName` — required for generic activities (see below). The API object name (e.g. `"Opportunity"`); ignored for concrete nodes.
17	   - `bodyParameters` — field-value pairs for the request body. Read field names from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`).
18	   - `queryParameters` — field-value pairs for query string parameters. Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: query` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
19	   - `pathParameters` — field-value pairs for path placeholders in `endpoint` (e.g. `{conversationsInfoId}`). Read from `connectorMethodInfo.parameters[]` where `type: path` (`registry get`) or `parameters[]` (`is resources describe`).
20	   - `filter` — structured FilterBuilder tree for list/query operations. See Step 6a.
21	   - `customFieldsRequestDetails` — design-time cache for connectors with an api-type ObjectAction at top-level `objectActions[]` OR `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`, Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`). camelCase keys; `parameterValues` as `[key, value]` tuples. See Step 6c.
22	   - `multipartParameters` — derived from IS metadata params where `type === "multipart"`. Array of `{name, dataType, value?}`. Pass file values via `--detail.bodyParameters.<name>`; `node configure` moves file-typed values into the matching `multipartParameters[i].value` slot (matched by `name`). String-typed entries — including the body aggregator field whose name is given by `inputMetadata.multipart.bodyFieldName` — stay in `bodyParameters`.
23	   - `inputMetadata` — auto-derived. `{type: "multipart", multipart: {bodyFieldName}}` when multipart params exist; `{operation: "list", pagination: {maxPageSize}}` for list operations. Driven by `methodInfo.parameters` + `methodInfo.operation`.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Generic vs Concrete Activities
28	
29	Connector nodes come in two flavors:
30	
31	- **Concrete** — the node type encodes a specific object + operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-atlassian-jira.curated_create_issue`). `inputDefinition.fields[]` is populated; `method` and `endpoint` are fixed.
32	- **Generic** — the node type encodes only the operation (e.g. `uipath.connector.uipath-salesforce-sfdc.list-records`, `…insert-record`, `…update-record`). `inputDefinition` is `{}`; the node needs an extra `objectName` in `--detail`, and `method` / `endpoint` come from `is resources describe`.
33	
34	To classify a node, read `Node.form.sections[0].fields[0].componentProps.connectorDetail.configuration` from the `registry get` response, parse it as JSON, and check `activityType`. `"Generic"` → run Step 2a to discover `objectName` (and capture `operation` from the same marker for the `--operation` flag in Step 3). Anything else → skip Step 2a.
35	
36	
37	## Critical: Connector Definition Must Include `form`
38	
39	> Connector definitions in `definitions[]` are CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)) — `uip maestro flow node add` copies them verbatim from the registry, and you should never hand-write or hand-edit them. If `node configure` fails with `No instanceParameters found in definition`, the definition in `definitions[]` is missing the `form` field — typically because the local registry cache is stale (the definition was copied in before the CLI started emitting `form`). Recovery: `uip maestro flow registry pull --force`, delete the stale `definitions[]` entry, re-run `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type>` so the CLI re-copies the definition with `form`. Do not paste `form` in by hand — re-running `node add` is the supported path.
40	
41	## No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration
42	
43	If you cannot run `node configure` (no live connection, sandbox forbids it, the user asked for planning only):
44	
45	1. Confirm the connector operation exists: `uip maestro flow registry search <keyword>` and `registry get <node-type>` (see [cli-commands.md — registry](../../../../shared/cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-registry) for the `search` output shape).
46	2. Add the connector node with `uip maestro flow node add <file> <node-type> --output json`. This is still required — it inserts the node and copies the definition into `definitions[]`. **Inside a loop body?** Add `--parent <LOOP_NODE_ID>` — see [loop/impl.md](../loop/impl.md).
47	3. Write the planned `--detail` payload to a separate file (e.g. `<nodeId>.detail.json`) with placeholder values for missing connection/folder UUIDs. Do **not** put a partial `inputs.detail` on the node.
48	4. **The node will not pass `flow validate` until `node configure` is run.** Surface this explicitly in your completion report under "Missing connections" or "Open questions" — do not let the user discover it via a validation failure later.
49	
50	Do not replace a registered connector operation with `core.logic.mock` because configuration cannot run. Mocks are only for genuinely unknown, unpublished, or not-yet-built non-connector resources. A real connector node added via `node add` but unconfigured preserves the registered connector key that Studio Web, reviewers, and downstream tooling need.
51	
52	When piping `--output json` into `python`, `jq`, or another parser, do not merge stderr into stdout. The CLI may emit diagnostic lines such as "Tool factory already registered..." before the JSON on stderr; use `2>/dev/null` for parse-only probes or capture stderr separately.
53	
54	## Configuration Workflow
55	
56	Follow these steps for every connector node.
57	
58	### Step 1 — Fetch and bind a connection
59	
60	Extract the connector key from the node type (`uipath.connector.<connector-key>.<activity-name>`).
61	
62	Discovery call is **always**:
63	
64	```bash
65	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
66	```
67	
68	`connections list` returns `Data` as a flat array. Do **not** parse `Data.Connections` or `Data.Items`; those wrapper objects are not part of the CLI JSON contract. Read each candidate from `Data[]` and use PascalCase fields:
69	
70	```json
71	{
72	  "Data": [
73	    {
74	      "Id": "<connection-id>",
75	      "Name": "<display-name>",
76	      "State": "Enabled",
77	      "IsDefault": "Yes",
78	      "Folder": "<folder-name>",
79	      "FolderKey": "<folder-key>"
80	    }
81	  ]
82	}
83	```
84	
85	Use `Data[i].Id` as the `--connection-id` value and `Data[i].FolderKey` as the `folderKey` value in `node configure --detail`.
86	
87	> **MUST READ before any `uip is connections ...` call:** [/uipath:uipath-platform — connections.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/connections.md). Single source of truth for selection rules (auto-select, personal workspace), BYOA filtering, empty-result recovery, ping verification.
88	
89	End state: a healthy connection `Id` + `FolderKey` for Step 2 (`registry get --connection-id`) and Step 6 (`node configure --detail`).
90	
91	### Step 2 — Get enriched node definitions with connection
92	
93	Call `registry get` with `--connection-id` to fetch connection-aware metadata including custom fields:
94	
95	```bash
96	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --connection-id <connection-id> --output json
97	```
98	
99	This returns enriched `inputDefinition.fields` and `outputDefinition.fields` with accurate type, required, description, enum, and `reference` info. Without `--connection-id`, only standard/base fields are returned.
100	
101	The response also includes `connectorMethodInfo` with the real HTTP `method` (e.g. `GET`, `POST`) and `path` template (e.g. `/ConversationsInfo/{conversationsInfoId}`). **Save `connectorMethodInfo.method` and `connectorMethodInfo.path`** — you must pass them to `node configure` later as `method` and `endpoint`.
102	
103	> **For generic activities, `connectorMethodInfo` is empty.** Method and endpoint are object-specific and only resolve once Step 2a picks an `objectName`; Step 3 then surfaces them via `availableOperations[]`. Don't try to derive them from the manifest alone.
104	
105	### Step 2a — Discover the object name (generic activities only)
106	
107	Skip this step for concrete activities — they encode the object in the node type. For generic activities (`activityType: "Generic"`), list the connection's catalog and pick the object the user wants to act on.
108	
109	```bash
110	uip is resources list "<connector-key>" --connection-id "<connection-id>" --output json \
111	  --output-filter "[?contains(DisplayName,'<search>')].{Name:Name,Path:Path,Custom:Custom}"
112	```
113	
114	- `Name` — what `--detail.objectName` accepts. Case-sensitive (e.g. `"Opportunity"`, not `"opportunity"`). Don't substitute `DisplayName`.
115	- `Path` — API endpoint suffix (e.g. `/Opportunity`). Pair with the operation's HTTP method (Step 3) for `endpoint`.
116	- `Custom` — `true` for tenant-defined objects.
117	
118	### Step 3 — Describe the resource and read full metadata
119	
120	Run `is resources describe` to fetch and cache the full operation metadata, then **read the cached metadata file** for complete field details including descriptions, types, references, and query/path parameters. The describe summary omits some of this.
121	
122	**Read `<objectName>` from the node definition in `definitions[]` (written by `node add`) — do not guess it from the node-type suffix.**
123	
124	```bash
125	# 1. Describe to trigger fetch + cache (objectName = the activity's API object, NOT the node-type suffix)
126	#    Read <objectName> from the node definition FIRST (see note below) — do not batch this
127	#    call with `node add` / `registry get`; those calls PRODUCE the objectName this one consumes.
128	uip is resources describe "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" \
129	  --connection-id "<id>" --operation Create --output json
130	# -> response includes metadataFile path
131	
132	# 2. Read the full cached metadata
133	cat <metadataFile path from response>
134	```
135	
136	> **`<objectName>` is the activity's API object name, not the node-type's trailing segment — and NOT a case-conversion of it.** Read it from the node definition copied into `definitions[]` by `node add`: `model.context[]` entry `{name:"objectName", value:"…"}` (or the `objectName` field inside the `configuration` `=jsonString:` blob). Never derive it by transforming the node-type suffix — kebab→snake (`send-email` → `send_email`) and kebab→Pascal are both guesses and both 404. Example: node type `…google-gmail.send-email` has objectName `SendEmail` (not `send_email`); `…teams.send-bot-direct-message` has objectName `bot_direct_messages` (not `send-bot-direct-message`). A 404 means wrong objectName — re-read it from the definition and retry; do NOT treat the 404 as "describe unavailable" and skip the step. Skipping describe loses `requestFields[].reference.filterPattern` and other IS-level metadata that `registry get` does not carry (see Step 4).
137	>
138	> **Sequence, don't parallelize, the objectName-dependent calls.** `<objectName>` is an OUTPUT of `node add` (it lands in `definitions[]`). Read that value before calling `is resources describe` — do not place `describe` in the same parallel Bash batch as `node add` or `registry get`, or you'll have nothing to pass but a guess. This is the failure mode behind the snake-case 404 above.
139	
140	The full metadata contains:
141	- **`availableOperations[].method`** and **`availableOperations[].path`** — HTTP method and API endpoint path. Same value as `connectorMethodInfo.method` / `.path` from `registry get`.
142	- **`parameters`** — query and path parameters (may include required params not in `requestFields`, e.g. `send_as` for Slack). Parameters carry `reference` objects too — scan them in Step 4 exactly like body fields.
143	- **`requestFields`** — body fields with `name`, `type`, `required`, `description`, and `reference` objects for ID resolution. Pair these field names with the `path` above (e.g. `messageToSend` for Slack `/send_message_to_channel_v2`).
144	- **`responseFields`** — response schema
145	
146	### Step 3a — Resolve parent-field-driven custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)
147	
148	**Run whenever the activity has a parent-field-driven schema** — an api-type ObjectAction in `objectActions[]` or `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` (see Step 6c's support table). Applies to **every** operation with such an action — Create/Edit/Update for parent-driven required body fields AND Get/Retrieve/Query for the response-schema fields downstream nodes will reference. The base `describe` returns only static metadata; this step runs the matching ObjectAction against the live connection so the cache you author in Step 6c is a replay of a real call, not a fabrication.
149	
150	Pass parent values via `-f, --field` — see [/uipath:uipath-platform — resources.md > Parent-Field-Driven Custom Fields (api-type ObjectActions)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/resources.md#parent-field-driven-custom-fields-api-type-objectactions) for the full procedure, flag table, merge semantics, and error recovery.

1	# UiPath Solution Workspace
2	
3	> **A `.uipx` file in this directory marks a UiPath solution. Drive every solution operation through the `uip` CLI — packing, publishing, deploying, and deployment configuration.** Do not hand-edit `.uipx`; manage projects via `uip solution projects ...` so the manifest stays internally consistent.
4	
5	This file is a static snapshot, scaffolded by the `uip` CLI version `1.201.0-dev.8272`. If the CLI version you have access to is different, there may be inconsistencies in the commands or options listed below. When you encounter one, look up the current form with `uip <group> --help` and **edit this file in place** — find and replace the stale command with the working one.
6	
7	## The `.uipx` Manifest
8	
9	`<solution>.uipx` is a JSON document at the solution root listing every project in the solution. Skeleton:
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	    "DocVersion": "1.0.0",
14	    "StudioMinVersion": "2025.10.0",
15	    "SolutionId": "<uuid>",
16	    "Projects": [
17	        {
18	            "Type": "Process",
19	            "ProjectRelativePath": "MyProcess/project.json",
20	            "Id": "<uuid>"
21	        }
22	    ]
23	}
24	```
25	
26	Typical layout:
27	
28	```text
29	my-solution/
30	    my-solution.uipx          ← solution manifest
31	    AGENTS.md                 ← this file (Codex, Cursor, generic agents)
32	    CLAUDE.md                 ← identical copy (Claude Code)
33	    ProjectA/
34	        project.json
35	        bindings_v2.json      ← per-project resource declarations
36	        ...
37	    ProjectB/
38	        project.uiproj
39	        ...
40	```
41	
42	You must manage membership via the CLI, never by editing the manifest. All these operations work entirely on local files (`.uipx` plus the solution-builder artefacts on disk) and do not require `uip login` — auth is only needed once you reach `pack` / `publish` / `deploy` / `upload`.
43	
44	| Intent | Command |
45	|---|---|
46	| Create a solution | `uip solution init <name>` |
47	| Register an existing subfolder of the solution dir as a project (no copying — use after scaffolding *inside* the solution dir, e.g. `uip rpa create-project --location <solution-dir>`) | `uip solution projects add <project-path> [<solution-file>]` |
48	| Add a project from outside the solution — copies the folder at `<path>` into the solution dir and registers it (`<path>` is a local filesystem path) | `uip solution projects import <path>` |
49	| Unregister a project (does not delete the project files on disk) | `uip solution projects remove <project-path> [<solution-file>]` |
50	| List projects in the solution | `uip solution projects list` |
51	
52	The `uip ... init` scaffolders (`agent init`, `maestro flow init`, `maestro bpmn init`, `maestro case init`, `api-workflow init`) **auto-register** the new project when run inside a solution directory — they walk up for the enclosing `.uipx` and add it to `Projects[]` automatically, so a separate `project add` is not needed. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to scaffold standalone without registering; the output's `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is then `OptedOut`. The full set of `Status` values is: `Registered` / `AlreadyRegistered` (added in this run / already present), `NotInSolution` (no enclosing `.uipx` found), `OptedOut` (`--skip-solution-registration` passed), `Skipped` (a candidate solution was found but registration was not safe to attempt — e.g. multiple `.uipx` in one directory, or the project sits outside the solution dir), and `Failed` (manifest read/parse/write error).
53	
54	## Project Types
55	
56	A solution can contain multiple projects of different types. The table below lists each project type and the `uip` command that scaffolds a fresh one (or marks the row when no scaffolding command exists).
57	
58	| Type | Description | Scaffold with | Skill |
59	|---|---|---|---|
60	| `Process` | RPA process — Studio workflow (XAML, Coded C#, or Hybrid) | `uip rpa create-project --name <name>` | `uipath-rpa` |

1	# IxP Extraction Node — Implementation
2	
3	IxP Extraction nodes invoke a published UiPath Intelligent eXtraction Platform (IxP) model. They are tenant-specific resources with pattern `uipath.ixp.{sanitized-modelName}.{sanitized-fullyQualifiedName}`.
4	
5	Sanitization rule (applied to both tail segments, in this order):
6	
7	1. Lowercase.
8	2. Replace runs of any character outside `[a-z0-9]` with a single `-`. Slashes, spaces, underscores, and runs of dashes (e.g. `---`) all collapse to a single `-`. Dots in the FQN are NOT preserved — they also collapse to `-`.
9	
10	The dot in `uipath.ixp.{model}.{fqn}` is the segment separator the registry adds *after* sanitizing each tail segment, not part of the sanitization itself.
11	
12	Examples (verified against the live registry):
13	
14	- `"birth_certificates_oob-6252526a-ixp"` + FQN `Shared/birth_certificates_oob-6252526a-ixp` → `uipath.ixp.birth-certificates-oob-6252526a-ixp.shared-birth-certificates-oob-6252526a-ixp` (underscores and slash both → `-`).
15	- `"idp-benchmark---invoices-c735405a-ixp"` + FQN `Shared/idp-benchmark---invoices-c735405a-ixp` → `uipath.ixp.idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp.shared-idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp` (run of `---` → single `-`).
16	
17	Always prefer the `nodeType` returned by `uip maestro flow registry search` over constructing one by hand.
18	
19	## Discovery
20	
21	```bash
22	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
23	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp" --output json
24	```
25	
26	Requires `uip login`. Only published IxP models from your tenant appear. Example returned `nodeType`: `uipath.ixp.idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp.shared-idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp` (for an `idp-benchmark---invoices-c735405a-ixp` model in the `Shared` folder).
27	
28	### Response shape
29	
30	`registry search` returns a top-level envelope; `Data` is a flat list of node entries (PascalCase keys):
31	
32	```json
33	{
34	  "Result": "Success",
35	  "Code": "NodeSearchSuccess",
36	  "Data": [
37	    {
38	      "NodeType": "uipath.ixp.idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp.shared-idp-benchmark-invoices-c735405a-ixp",
39	      "Category": "document-processing",
40	      "DisplayName": "idp-benchmark---invoices-c735405a-ixp",
41	      "Description": "(Shared)",
42	      "Version": "1.0.0",
43	      "Tags": "ixp, document-understanding, extraction"
44	    }
45	  ]
46	}
47	```
48	
49	Read entries as `raw["Data"][i]["NodeType"]` (not `raw["Data"]["Nodes"]`).
50	
51	### If `Data` is empty → stop and use a mock
52	
53	If `uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp"` returns `Data: []`, **no IxP extraction model is published on this tenant**. Add a `core.logic.mock` placeholder node (see [If the Model Does Not Exist Yet](#if-the-model-does-not-exist-yet)) and surface the missing model in **Open Questions**.
54	
55	**Stop searching.** Do not run any of these as a fallback:
56	
57	- Domain-keyword searches: `registry search "invoice"`, `"form"`, `"document"`, `"W-9"`, `"receipt"`, `"contract"`, etc. — there is no domain-named extraction node; IxP is the only extraction primitive.
58	- `registry list` followed by client-side filtering for "ixp" / "extraction" — the strict `uipath.ixp` search is already authoritative.
59	- Variant-prefix searches: `registry search "uipath.agent.resource.tool.ixp"`, `"core.ixp"`, etc.
60	
61	The fallback is `core.logic.mock`, full stop. At most run one broader `registry search "ixp"` to confirm there are no `uipath.ixp.*` hits hidden by stricter prefix matching, then mock.
62	
63	> A `uipath.agent.resource.tool.ixp.*` hit on the broader `"ixp"` search is the *agent-tool* variant — not a flow extraction node. Treat it as "no extraction model published" and fall back to mock.
64	
65	## Listing Published Models
66	
67	When the user is working with a Maestro flow and asks what IxP models are available — "what IxP models can I access in Maestro?", "what IxP models / runtime projects can I use in this flow?", "what document extractors can I add here?", "list published extractors", "what extraction nodes are in the registry?" — answer with the same registry search **from the `uipath-maestro-flow` Skill**, not by switching to the `uipath-ixp` Skill (`uip ixp projects ...` lists IxP-product projects, not what is wired up for Maestro). Each `Data[]` entry corresponds to one published model (a.k.a. runtime project) visible to the flow registry on this tenant.
68	
69	```bash
70	uip login status --output json                              # confirm auth — without login, tenant IxP nodes are hidden
71	uip maestro flow registry pull --force
72	uip maestro flow registry search "uipath.ixp" --output json
73	```
74	
75	Parse `Data[].DisplayName`, `Data[].NodeType`, and `Data[].Version` and present them as a table. Example:
76	
77	| Model (DisplayName) | NodeType | Version |

82	
83	- **Do NOT scaffold a solution, run `uip maestro flow init`, or write a `.flow` file.** Listing is read-only Q&A.

85	- **Do NOT log in for the user.** If `uip login status` shows logged-out, tell the user to run `uip login` and stop — listing without auth returns OOTB-only results and is misleading.

88	- **Do NOT guess `uip maestro flow list-*` or `uip maestro ixp list-*` subcommands.** None exist. The CLI returns `unknown command 'list-...'` and there is no fallback path to pursue. <!-- uip-check-skip -->

90	## Registry Validation
91	
92	```bash
93	uip maestro flow registry get "<node-type>" --output json
94	```
95	
96	Confirm:
97	
98	- `category` — `document-processing` (older `document-extraction` enum was renamed; current registry serves `document-processing`)
99	- Input port: `input`
100	- Output ports: `success` and `error` (the `error` port is gated by `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled`; manifest sets `supportsErrorHandling: true`). Edges target these handle IDs in `.flow` JSON; `handleType` is `output`.

100	- Output ports: `success` and `error` (the `error` port is gated by `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled`; manifest sets `supportsErrorHandling: true`). Edges target these handle IDs in `.flow` JSON; `handleType` is `output`.
101	- `model.type` — `bpmn:ServiceTask`. `model.serviceType` — `IXP.Extraction`. The manifest's `model` is two fields only (`type`, `serviceType`) — no `context`, no `version`. Both are injected by the BPMN serializer at compile time.
102	- `form.id` — `ixp-standalone-form`. Three sections: `ixp-model` (Configuration), `ixp-file-upload` (File input), `schema-definition` (Schema definition — a single custom field `inputs.model` rendered by the `ixp-model-taxonomy` component).
103	- `inputDefinition.properties` — `model` (object), `modelName`, `projectName`, `projectId`, `versionTag`, `folderKey`, `folderName`, `fileRef`, `pageRange`, `attachmentConfig`, `guardrails`, `attachment`. `inputDefinition.required` — `["fileRef"]`.
104	- `inputDefaults` — carries the full `model` metadata blob plus flat `modelName` / `projectName` / `folderKey` / `folderName` mirrors. The deployment-node blob shape is `{ id, modelName, modelDisplayName, folderKey, folderName, folderPath, description }`. Note: `model.modelName` is frequently `null` for published/OOB deployments — the human name is in `model.modelDisplayName` (and mirrored in the flat `inputDefaults.modelName`). See Authoring rule #1.
105	- `outputDefinition` — populated. `output` carries the full extraction-result JSON schema; `error` carries the standard error envelope.
